state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: What would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem with just two plants?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so if I take just two plants, like one that's \( 10 \mathrm{~cm} \) and another that's \( 20 \mathrm{~cm} \), the range is \( 20 - 10 = 10 \mathrm{~cm} \). If I cut both in half, they would be \( 5 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 10 \mathrm{~cm} \), and the range would still be \( 10 - 5 = 5 \mathrm{~cm} \). But if I add \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to both, they'd be \( 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 23 \mathrm{~cm} \), and the range is still \( 23 - 13 = 10 \mathrm{~cm} \). So, I guess I see what you mean, but why does it change when you cut them in half

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: What would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem with just two plants, but this time the heights are closer together, like \( 12 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 15 \mathrm{~cm} \)?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so if I take the two plants that are \( 12 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 15 \mathrm{~cm} \), the range is \( 15 - 12 = 3 \mathrm{~cm} \). If I cut them in half, they would be \( 6 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 7.5 \mathrm{~cm} \), and the range would be \( 7.5 - 6 = 1.5 \mathrm{~cm} \). So it looks like the range changes when I cut them in half, but I still don't get why it doesn't change when I add the same amount. Can you explain that part again?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the misconception by guiding the student through carefully chosen examples that reveal why multiplication changes range while addition doesn't, leading the student to discover the pattern independently and correct their initial error.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student toward self-discovery, never directly provides answers, and effectively employs counterexamples (simpler cases with different numbers) to help the student expose the flaw in their own reasoning.
